lexingCheck: Token streams are hand-derived (harness/vector_sources.py); check_vectors.py re-lexes every input with pylex.py and checks layout, keyword, operator, number and prefix rules on the recorded stream; harness/crosscheck.py compares them with the CPython 3.14.6 tokenizer.

vectors.description: Empty input: zero tokens, insufficient-tokens, no k-grams.
Four tokens (NEWLINE included), fewer than k=5.
Exactly k=5 tokens: one exact k-gram, partial window.
Period-2 repetition: equal hashes in one window; the rightmost wins.
Comment and blank lines only: no NEWLINE, no INDENT, zero tokens.
Comment/whitespace pair, plain layout.
vectors.inputText:
def f(a, b):
    return a + b

vectors.description: Same tokens as py-format-a: CRLF, a comment inside the brackets, a blank and a comment-only line, tab indentation and trailing white space.
vectors.inputText:
def f(a,   # first
      b):

	# about the body
	return a+b

vectors.description: Rename pair, original names and literals.
Rename pair: other names, number and quote style.
Re-indentation pair, 4-space levels.
Same block structure with a tab level and a tab-plus-two-spaces level: identical tokens and hashes.
Line-joining pair: one physical line.
Same logical line split with two backslash continuations: identical tokens and hashes.
Two statements joined by ';' on one line.
The same two statements on two lines (the black/ruff layout).
Blank and comment-only lines at any indentation do not change the indentation stack.
vectors.inputText:
if x:
    a = 1
# top-level comment

        # deeper comment
    b = 2

vectors.description: Inside brackets, line terminators, comments and blank lines produce no NEWLINE and no indentation.
vectors.inputText:
x = f(a,
      b,

  # note
      c)
y = [1,
2]

vectors.description: A backslash continuation inside a compound-statement header.
A continuation joined to an empty line: the empty line's terminator ends the logical line.
Lone CR ends a physical line (the 'Classic Mac OS' form).
Backslash followed by CR LF is one continuation, not a continuation and a line end.
A form feed in leading white space resets the column count: '  \f  y' is at column 2, like '  z'.
Between tokens a form feed is white space.
Indentation is the white space up to the first backslash (4 here), not the white space after it.
Departure D-3: a continuation at column 0 gives indentation 0 (reference); CPython 3.14.6 counts the next line's spaces and emits INDENT.
Tab then spaces: column 12 at tab size 8 and 5 at tab size 1, both greater than the tab level.
No final line terminator: NEWLINE and two DEDENTs at the end of input.
DEDENT is zero-width at the first byte of the dedented line's first token, not at the line start.
NEWLINE is zero-width at the line terminator, after a trailing comment.
A fragment whose first line is indented: INDENT first, DEDENT at the end (the parser would reject it).
Type comments are ordinary comments.
A shebang line and a UTF-8 coding declaration are comments.
A non-UTF-8 declaration on an all-ASCII file: the declaration is a comment and the bytes lex as UTF-8.
Hard keywords, including True/False/None and async/await.
vectors.inputText:
async def f():
    await g()
    return None or True and not False

vectors.description: match, case, type and _ are ident in every position, as statements and as names.
vectors.inputText:
match = re.match(p, s)
match command:
    case [x, _]:
        type X = int

vectors.description: Non-ASCII names: no normalization; the fullwidth spelling of 'if' and the ligature 'fi' are ident (CPython classes keywords on the raw text and NFKC-normalizes only later).
Departure D-8: U+A7CE is XID_Start in the pinned Unicode 17.0.0 tables; CPython 3.14.6 (Unicode 16.0.0) rejects it.
Longest match over the reference operator and delimiter list.
Departure D-5: '<>' is not in the reference operator list, so it is '<' '>'; CPython's tokenizer returns one OP '<>' (barry_as_FLUFL).
Dots: '..' is two tokens, '. 5' is a dot and an int, '.5' a float.
Every integer form, floats with leading zeros, exponents, imaginary literals.
A number directly followed by a keyword (SyntaxWarning in 3.14, not an error), and by 'if' + letters.
vectors.inputText:
x = 1if y else 2
z = 0x1for w in v
u = 1ifx

vectors.description: '1..real' is float '1.' then '.'; '1 .real' is int then '.'.
A number followed by a name character.
Leading zeros in a non-zero decimal integer.
Two underscores in a row.
'0o' with no octal digit is an error even though 'or' follows ('0or').
'or' must be a whole word after a number: '1orx' is an error, unlike '1ifx'.
An exponent letter with no digits.
A digit directly after an imaginary literal.
'1.real': the float '1.' is followed by a name character.
Every prefix family in mixed case; b gives class bytes; empty and empty triple-quoted strings.
Escaped quote, escaped backslash and backslash-newline inside single-quoted strings.
Escape validity and the ASCII-only rule for bytes are not lexical (D-4): accepted as written.
In a raw string a backslash still takes the next character: r'\'' is one string, r"\\" another.
A triple-quoted string with newlines, lone quotes and the other quote kind inside.
Adjacent literals stay separate tokens (concatenation is the parser's job).
A name before a quote is a prefix only if it is distinct prefix letters: uu, rr, print and bx are names.
'u' and 'r' are incompatible (a 3.14 tokenizer error).
'f' and 'b' are incompatible, in any case.
A line terminator inside a single-quoted string.
A lone CR ends the line inside a string.
End of input inside a triple-quoted string.
A raw string cannot end in an odd backslash.
Literal runs, a conversion, a format spec with a nested field, and '{{' '}}' kept inside one middle token.
PEP 701: the outer quote reused inside a field, and an f-string nested in a field.
Debug '=', a conversion after '=', ':' starting a spec before ':=' can match, and a parenthesized ':='.
A single-quoted f-string whose field spans lines and holds a comment: no NEWLINE inside.
'\N{...}' is literal text in a non-raw f-string; in a raw one '\N' is text and '{y}' a field.
A backslash before '{' is text and the brace opens a field.
In a triple-quoted f-string a format spec may hold a line break.
In a format spec '{' always opens a field: '{{z}}' is a field holding a set display.
Departure D-6: the same rule after a nested field; CPython 3.14.6 reads '{{' there as an escape.
t-strings (3.14) lex like f-strings with their own classes.
A single '}' in literal text.
A line terminator in the literal text of a single-quoted f-string.
A line terminator in the format spec of a single-quoted f-string.
Inside a field the quote starts a new string, which is unterminated.
')' where the field's '}' is expected.
Tab and 8 spaces: equal at tab size 8, different at tab size 1: inconsistent.
Deeper at tab size 8 (9 > 8) but not at tab size 1 (2 <= 8): inconsistent.
A dedent to a level that is not on the stack.
Four spaces then a tab is column 8; a later tab-only line is column 8 too but differs at tab size 1.
'$' is an error (reference); CPython's tokenizer returns OP and only the parser rejects it.
U+00A0 is not white space.
U+2E2F is Lm but not XID_Continue.
U+000B (VT) is a control character, not white space.
A backslash not followed by a line terminator.
A continuation whose line terminator is the last thing in the input.
A closer that does not match the opener.
End of input with brackets open: the innermost opener.
A byte that is not UTF-8.
A latin-1 declaration does not change decoding: the byte E9 is not UTF-8 (CPython decodes it as latin-1).
A leading BOM is rejected (shared contract rule OD-1).
NUL is rejected anywhere (contract §3; also CPython 3.12+).
